title: One-Shot Disable-Switch Clearance Policy for Guarded Canary
summary: Record the policy decision for the final deliberate execution blocker after FP-MCP-227 produced valid approval evidence and valid operator-local clearance, while guarded preflight remained blocked only by the deliberate disable/execution-enable policy. The disable switch must not become a standing enable mode. Any future clearance must be one-shot, tuple-bound, and self-revoking: validate the request artifact, approval, operator-local clearance, and guarded preflight; clear execution only for the exact validated attempt; contact the runner start endpoint at most once; record approval consumption and pre/post state; then immediately restore disabled state or otherwise make the tuple unusable for any second attempt. This packet is a policy decision only and does not implement or perform execution enablement.
caveats: The FP-MCP-227 approval and operator-local clearance were valid at observation time but are time-boxed and may expire before implementation is ready.
The existing local clearance artifact expires at 2026-07-03T13:22:30.944357Z and must not be reused after expiry.
The existing approval expires at 2026-07-03T13:30:00.000Z and must not be consumed after expiry.
No standing execution authority is approved by this policy.
No generic global disable-switch clearing tool is approved.
The next implementation must preserve FP-MCP-217: execution authorization remains human-local and outside the model-callable MCP surface; MCP may observe/validate but must not create local clearance.
If implementation cannot complete before expiry, a fresh approval and fresh local clearance must be created and observed before any canary attempt.
